Remarks: The water's sweet. Somebody did that with their own two hands.
First summer in years nobody's boiled the well water.
Conditions.Heard: They say Sill's well runs clear now. A stranger rebuilt the ring by hand.

Remarks: The Concord's man came round for the well money again.
Clean water, and a bill nailed by the door for it.
Conditions.Heard: Sill pays the Concord for its own water now, I hear.

Remarks: Bread every morning again. Smell that.
The oven's fine. The Concord's inspector says so, every season, for a fee.
The watch can see the bend in the road all night now.
Conditions.Heard: Sill keeps a proper light on its road again. Safer going that way.

Remarks: That sealed lantern of the Concord's never gutters. Nobody here knows how it works.
Perch in the nets again. The weir's holding.
The old men are down at the weir arguing about it again. Let them be.
Conditions.Heard: Tine's weir is mended, they say. There'll be perch on the boats this season.

Remarks: The Concord's weir works. So does the Concord's catch-tax.
The scribe finished her copy. She says the gap in it is the best part.
The scribe has a new margin in her copy. She read it to us twice.
Conditions.Heard: The old copyist at Tine has entered the third hand. Someone carried it to her.

Remarks: The registrar entered six crates. The drover's allowed to stand up now.
Conditions.Heard: Cloth caravans will go through Gantry again. Their registrar counted six.

Remarks: The exchange floor is smiling at everybody. Somebody signed something for them.
Conditions.Heard: Gantry signed a short count against a caravan of the cloth. Go through there with your crates where you can see them.

Remarks: There is shade under the cloth again. Sit.
Conditions.Heard: A stranger rehung the guest-cloth at Gantry. The oath keeps there.

Remarks: The guest bowl is full. Someone saw to it.
No more paying for a bridge nobody built.
Conditions.Heard: Sill's road-tithe has a new hand on the roll: no bridge, nothing owing. First new hand on that roll in years.

Remarks: We've stopped paying the bridge money. Let them come and show us the bridge.
We paid the bridge money. There's still no bridge.
